cells.tense: Right now, the load you are bearing rests on ground that is not running down.
cells.act: envision it freshly and feel toward it
cells.ask: Set aside a few minutes to sense what hasn't happened yet — some next thing, felt toward with real curiosity, no plan attached. Then let it be.
cells.core:
Right now, the load you bear rests on something that isn't running down. That's the quiet fact of it: you can hold weight without going stiff, and keep wanting the very thing you're carrying while you hold it. Nothing here needs proving to anyone. It holds, and you keep going. When it's going its way, you get to look ahead without flinching, because the ground under you is solid enough to want from.

So give a little room to what hasn't happened yet. Sit with some next thing for a few minutes and feel toward it — curious, not decided, no plan and no one to tell. That's the whole of it. You don't need to know how it lands. Let the wanting be there while the ground is solid.
cells.sheetLine: The ground holds, so you can want what comes next.

cells.place: where the weight is carried and held

cells.tense: A moment ahead of you has not arrived, and you are already carrying its weight.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Bring out the sentence you keep rehearsing for a future talk. Say it plainly to whoever it concerns, once, warm and simple, then leave it alone.
cells.core:
A moment ahead of you hasn't happened, and you're carrying it anyway, turning it over so nothing catches you off guard. That's what the load is made of now: things that might go wrong, gone over in advance. People feel the weight even when you say nothing about it. What it costs is the present, spent early on a day you can't write yet.

The way out isn't less care. Say the sentence you've been rehearsing. Not to brace them — just to say it, once, plainly, to whoever it concerns. Then leave it alone. The ground under you is the same as it was before you started bracing.

cells.tense: There was a threshold you crossed a while back, and some part of you never left it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Stop feeding a finished thing — an old plan, a role, an evening worry. Quit the checking and the picking back up, and leave your hands free for what's live.
cells.core:
A threshold got crossed some time back, and part of you stayed at the doorway instead of coming through. Not deciding, not leaving — parked where you already are. Meanwhile your arms are full: plans finished a year ago, roles you said you'd carry a bit longer, worries that arrive every evening. You're still upright. You've simply got no hand free.

So put something down. Take a finished thing — a plan, a role, a worry you keep feeding — and stop tending it: no more checking, no more lifting it back up. Not because it wasn't real. Because it's done, and your hands are wanted elsewhere.
cells.sheetLine: Your arms are full of things already finished.

cells.tense: The steady push is underway right now, and the tally you keep files it under circumstance.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Make a visible change to something you keep meaning to shift — a single real inch, small enough to finish, with nothing planned beyond it.
cells.core:
The steady push is underway. Something around you keeps shifting because you keep showing up to it — the daily version, unglamorous and relentless. When it's working, a thing changes under your hands and you know exactly why, since you did the showing up. But that's not how the story gets told. It comes out as luck or timing. It came from somewhere, and you know the work that went in.

Here's the small correction. Make a visible change to something you keep meaning to shift — a single real inch, small enough to finish. No plan for beyond it. Then the change carries your name too.
cells.sheetLine: The push is yours. The record keeping isn't.

attempts.check: The draft keeps wanting to say the person keeps others' fires lit, which the record does not say — the signature is Drive as behavior, and in this seat it is read through bearing, not through what they give anybody else. A reader could rightly say they're the one being carried and no fire of theirs is tended by anyone, so no ask may turn on another person's momentum or on anyone's gratitude. The asks survive that: each one is a bodily act on a load of their own, useful even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them is the warm reversal line about being met partway — it costs them nothing and buys me depth, so it goes.
